documents.title: Sunridge Solar Farm Begins Operation
documents.text: DELANO (July 21) - The Sunridge Solar Farm, the largest in the state, began feeding electricity into the grid on Monday. [A] The 120-megawatt facility covers 800 acres of former farmland and contains more than 300,000 panels. [B] According to operator Brightpath Energy, it will generate enough power for about 30,000 homes and cut carbon emissions by an estimated 150,000 tons a year. [C] The $190 million project created 450 jobs during construction, but only 12 permanent positions will remain, a fact that some local officials have criticized. [D] To address those concerns, Brightpath has promised to fund a technical training program at Delano Community College and to give hiring priority to program graduates.

documents.text:
To: All Employees
From: Human Resources
Date: October 21

Open enrollment runs from November 1 to November 15. During this period, you may change your health, dental, and vision plans for next year. If you do not make changes, your current selections will continue, except for the Basic Health plan, which will be replaced by Standard Health with a monthly premium that is $14 higher. A new option, the Wellness Plus plan, adds coverage for gym memberships and counseling at no extra cost over the Standard plan. To enroll, log in to the benefits portal using your employee ID. Employees who want to add dependents must upload supporting documents, such as a birth certificate, by November 8. Information sessions will be held in the main conference room on October 30 at noon and 6 p.m.

documents.title: Westbury Library Introduces Self-Checkout
documents.text: WESTBURY (February 12) - Starting Monday, Westbury Public Library patrons will be able to check out their own books using four new self-service kiosks. [A] The machines, which cost $38,000, were funded by a donation from the Friends of the Library. [B] Library director Elaine Burke said the change will shorten lines during busy afternoon hours and free staff to help with research and children's programs. [C] Staff members will remain at the front desk to assist patrons who prefer a personal checkout or have difficulty with the machines. [D] Cardholders can also use the kiosks to pay fines and print receipts. The library, which circulates about 400,000 items a year, will hold demonstrations every Saturday in February at 11 a.m.

documents.title: Council Approves Plan to Close Fenwick Park Road
documents.text: GLENMORE (August 14) - The Glenmore City Council voted Monday to close Fenwick Park Road to cars on weekends from May to October, creating a car-free promenade along the river. The pilot program, which begins next spring, will cost an estimated $85,000 for barriers, signs, and event staffing. Supporters, including the Glenmore Cycling Club, say it will encourage exercise and boost sales at nearby cafés. Some residents of the road, however, worry about access for visitors and emergency vehicles. The council said emergency access will be maintained and that residents will receive free weekend parking permits for nearby lots. The program will be reviewed after one season.

documents.title: Letter to the Editor
documents.text:
To the Editor:
I live on Fenwick Park Road and am writing about the council's decision. I support the idea of a car-free promenade; my family bikes there often. But I am concerned about my elderly parents, who visit on Sundays and cannot walk far. Free permits for distant lots will not help them. I urge the council to allow short-term drop-offs at the front of my building. I also hope that the review after one season includes residents' opinions.
Sincerely,
Hannah Cole

choices: Her family enjoys biking along the road
She works for the cycling club
questions.explanation: She writes that her family bikes there often.

questions.explanation: Her elderly parents cannot walk far from a distant parking lot.
